+## P-AK-SEARCH-1-A3.1 — the A3 epoch is the measurement epoch (RATIFIED 2026-09-26)
+Appended to Annex K as a clarification of `P-AK-SEARCH-1-A3` Clause 1. It supersedes nothing in
+A3's text. It fixes what "declared host state" includes, and leaves every other part of A3, of
+`P-AK-SEARCH-1`, and of the owning release protocols untouched. Operator decision OP-60,
+### What Clause 1 said, and what the implementation did
+Clause 1 defines an epoch as the SHA-256 of "the anchor commit, the build recipe, and the declared
+host state, taken together". It does not name actor configuration. The implementation folded the
+campaign's actor roster into host state anyway: `host_state` carried `enrolled_manifest_digest`, the
+digest of the whole resolved campaign manifest, and that manifest includes the `actors` and
+`fallbacks` blocks. So every change to who plans, authors or critiques moved the epoch.
+Both readings are recorded here, because they decide whether this is an amendment or a
+clarification:
+- **The text.** "Anchor commit, build recipe, declared host state" names three measured inputs.
+  Actor configuration is not one of them. On this reading the implementation over-reached and this
+  section is a **clarification**.
+- **The implementation.** Actor configuration lived inside `host_state` from the day A3 shipped,
+  and every A3 epoch recorded so far includes it. On this reading this section **changes** the
+  epoch that A3 records carry.
+The operator's ruling takes the first reading. This section is written as a clarification, and it
+states the change in recorded epochs so that nothing depends on the choice of label.
+### Clause 1a — the epoch is the measurement epoch
+The epoch in A3 Clauses 1 and 2 is the **measurement epoch**: the SHA-256 of
+- the anchor commit;
+- the build recipe;
+- the declared host state, which is every input that decides what is built, run and measured: the
+  CPU and GPU execution digests, the frozen request set, the enrolled target, the campaign
+  manifest's measured content (the manifest minus its actor roster), the CPU screen scope and the
+  serving instrument.
+It **excludes** actor configuration:
+- the planner, author and critic models and backends;
+- their reasoning efforts, thinking settings, context and output limits, and prompt knobs;
+- the manifest's `actors` and `fallbacks` blocks, and any digest that folds them in.
+The reference implementation is `ResolvedCampaign.measurement_digest` and `measurement_epoch` in
+`epyc-inference-research` (`scripts/kernel_rnd/autokernel/loop/campaign.py` and `loop/run.py`,
+research main `d643d794`). It replaces `enrolled_manifest_digest` with the manifest's
+`measurement_digest` and hashes the same anchor, recipe and remaining host state.
+### Clause 1b — what keys on it
+- **Planner-history comparability.** Records that share a measurement epoch MAY be ranked against
+  each other under Clause 1, whichever actors produced them. A record from a different measurement
+  epoch falls under Clause 2: it is evidence of attempt, never of magnitude.
+- **The do-not-repeat gate.** A mechanism already measured under the current measurement epoch
+  counts as measured, whichever actor authored the patch. An actor change does not re-admit it.
+  Narrower hypotheses and governed re-entry remain legal exactly as before.
+### Clause 1c — legacy rows fail closed
+A record that does not carry its measurement identity (rows written before the measurement epoch
+existed) MUST NOT be presumed to share one. It is compared on the full epoch only. If its full
+epoch differs, it is cross-epoch under Clause 2. It is never promoted to "same epoch" by inference.
+### Why
+A measured speed or correctness result does not depend on which actor authored the patch. The
+patch is the measured object, and it is identified per record rather than by the epoch. Under the
+full epoch, every actor change hid prior same-anchor results from the planner and re-admitted
+mechanisms that had already been measured. There were four actor changes in the week
+ending 2026-09-26. One critic swap moved the full epoch from `e0aefe6a` to `e384c2ad`, with the anchor,
+target, recipe, instrument, requests and floor all unchanged. Resume checkpoints already bind on
+the measurement epoch for the same reason (research lane `ak-author-medium`, `3cbdccea`). This
+section gives comparability and the do-not-repeat gate the same identity.
+### What this does not change
+- The full epoch is still recorded. It remains the provenance key for archive rows, history and
+  status. This section changes which identity comparison uses, not what is recorded.
+- A change to any measured input still moves the measurement epoch. That includes the anchor, the
+  recipe, an execution digest, the request set, the target, the screen scope and the instrument.
+- If an actor setting ever changes what is built or measured, and not only who proposes, it is a
+  measured input and belongs in the measurement epoch.
+- Every denial in *"What this protocol does NOT authorize"*, every precondition, the campaign
+  calibration block and the release boundary stand exactly as A3 left them.
